note: Clock time: “prayed that night until five o'clock” rendered “hadi saa tano”, keeping the printed hour number per house rule. In Swahili time-keeping saa tano reads as 11 a.m.; the English means 5 a.m. (Swahili time: saa kumi na moja alfajiri). Reviewer may wish to adjust.

Idiom: “the wolf … scratched at the cabin door” (poverty at the door) rendered with the sense “njaa … ilikuwa ikikwaruza mlango wa kibanda” (hunger scratching at the door); the literal wolf is opaque in Swahili.
Idiom: Kelly's “Religion is not my long suit” (card-playing idiom) rendered by sense: “Dini si fani yangu” (religion is not my field).

Baseball terms rendered by sense: “sandlots” → viwanja vya mtaani; “bleachers” → mashabiki; “the diamond” → uwanja wa besiboli; “stealing home” → kujirusha kunyakua kituo cha nyumbani (sliding to take home plate). Swahili readers may not know baseball base terminology.

Heading “A curbstone recruit” rendered “Aliyeandikishwa kando ya barabara” (one enlisted at the roadside), keeping the enlistment image that echoes his soldier father; the baseball sense of ‘recruit’ is lost.
“hitting the sawdust trail” rendered “kuikanyaga njia ya machujo ya mbao” (treading the sawdust path), used consistently in long and short bio; tabernacles → maskani (the SUV word for tabernacle).
“John Barleycorn” (personification of liquor) kept as a name in quotation marks, no gloss added; Swahili readers may not recognise it.
“One Sunday afternoon” — the play on his surname (Sunday) is lost in Swahili (Jumapili).
Sermon title “Teach Us to Pray” kept in English, as the Smith Wigglesworth bio keeps English book titles.
Prohibition rendered “marufuku ya vileo”, matching the term already used in the shipped Swahili bios.
Luke 18:13: English has “God be merciful to me a sinner!”; the SUV wording includes the vocative “Ee Mungu”, which is the standard Swahili rendering of the address, not an addition.
